# UICC, USIM and the card interface: compliance register

What this is: the requirements of this area that are built and verified against running code, the typed rows recorded while building them, and coverage counts derived from the specs (verification.md §5). Requirements are in [`requirements.md`](../../requirements.md); deviations in [`deviations.md`](../deviations.md).

Specs read: TS 102.221 18.04.00, TS 31.101 j00, TS 31.102 j60.

Row suffixes (requirements.md): -D defect in the sim, -B a choice the spec leaves open, -G declared gap, -V deviation from a "shall", -S spec contradiction and the reading chosen, -M mutant, -T T0 reading or measurement, -F a kaluza-core defect the sim found, -X retired. Verification: U unit, KAT or oracle test; F fuzz or property test; I interop; L lab; G gate row; A real-device comparison.

| KS-UICC-T2 | 2026-10-14 | Oracle defects seen in M12. pySim computes a READ/UPDATE BINARY offset as ((P1 & 0x7F) << 8) & P2 where TS 102 221 11.1.3.2 means P1's low bits and P2 together (an OR): its reading is checked against its own formula and tshark's bin_offset against ours (they agree). tshark 4.6.4 reads a P3 of '00' (Le 256) and the next octet as a two-octet extended Le, so Le 256 is not compared with it. | KS-UICC-B2 | 2026-10-15 | The soft card as built in P1 N3 (sim-uicc.md sections 2-7). The card OS takes command APDUs and answers response APDUs with T=0 semantics on by default: a command without Le whose answer has data gets 61xx and GET RESPONSE; a wrong Le gets 6Cxx; GSM-class 'A0' commands get 6E00. Access rules are evaluated in the expanded format (AM_DO then SC_DOs: always, never, a key reference, OR and AND templates) from the EF.ARR named in each file's '8B'. Key files (AF20) hold their contents as SecretBytes and are never read out; the EFs that hold session keys (4F03, 4F05) persist only in the sealed secrets file, never in the YAML image. The USIM application runs AUTHENTICATE with Milenage or TUAK from AF20 and the Annex C SQN check from AF30, both in sysmoISIM's layouts so one burn path serves soft and real cards. Card secrets (K, OPc, PINs, ADM1, sealed EFs) live in a file sealed with AES-256-GCM under a 32-octet KEK from a 0600 file; K and OPc of a sim-range IMSI derive as the first 16 octets of HMAC-SHA-256(master, label \|\| IMSI). The terminal is the ME's side: power-on, EF.DIR to the USIM AID, reads sized from the FCP, AUTHENTICATE returning CK and IK as SecretBytes; APDU buffers that carried keys or PINs are wiped.
